repository.name: geckolib
repository.description: GeckoLib is an animation engine for Minecraft mods, with support for complex 3D keyframe-based animations, numerous easings, concurrent animation support, sound and particle keyframes, event keyframes, math-based animations, and more. Available for all major modloaders.

issues.title: Geckolib Doesn't Recognize Aliases
issues.body:
Disclaimer: I'm not sure if this a bug or just not a feature.
### Issue:
When writing code, it's shorter and easier to use aliases such as `q` for `query` and `v` for `variable` as displayed here: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/minecraft/creator/documents/molang/syntax-guide?view=minecraft-bedrock-stable#:~:text=Alias%20mapping,Expand%20table

Though, from in-game testing, Geckolib doesn't recognize `q` as `query`.
So either this is not a feature, or it is a bug I'm not sure.
If it's not a bug then I'd like you to mark this as a suggestion.

issues.title: Valid animations getting dropped due to concurrency bug?
issues.body: The easiest way to reproduce this for me is with the following mod list (4.9.2 vs 4.9.3 still produces the crash): and then placing and naming a Player Statue from Iron's Lib (right click with an `Iron431` nametag). Log: https://mclo.gs/vCBwY4Z (loaded into a working world, exited, loaded into a world with a named Iron's Lib statue in blockentity render distance) > [!WARNING] > Speculation beyond this point. What I think is happening here is Ars Additions has enough valid animations and Marvel Legacy has enough invalid/non-Gecko animations to expose a concurrency bug, but I don't know for sure. I believe it's due to this composition being a `thenRunAsync` instead of a `thenCompose`, which means `loadAnimations` doesn't wait for `loadResources` to finish: https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/cce098097cdd2084d8383bec593e0db79e0ed5a0/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/cache/GeckoLibCache.java#L76-L77 Which means the global animation map is getting queried before being fully filled: https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/cce098097cdd2084d8383bec593e0db79e0ed5a0/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/cache/GeckoLibCache.java#L66-L69 I'm short on time right now, but if geckolib is easy to build, in a few days I can test this change myself and report back.

issues.title: IllegalStateException "Image is not allocated" in GeckoLibAnimatedTexture.tick() after a resource reload (language change)
issues.body:
**Environment**
- GeckoLib 5.5.6 (geckolib-neoforge-26.2)
- Minecraft 26.2, NeoForge 26.2.0.88
- Windows, dev environment

**What happens**
Changing the language in the options while in a world (this triggers a resource reload) crashes the client with:

java.lang.IllegalStateException: Image is not allocated.
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.platform.NativeImage.checkAllocated(NativeImage.java:174)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.platform.NativeImage.getPixelABGR(NativeImage.java:218)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.platform.NativeImage.getPixel(NativeImage.java:224)
    at com.geckolib.renderer.texture.GeckoLibAnimatedTexture$AnimationInfo$InterpolationData.getPixel(GeckoLibAnimatedTexture.java:292)
    at com.geckolib.renderer.texture.GeckoLibAnimatedTexture$AnimationInfo$InterpolationData.tickAndUpload(GeckoLibAnimatedTexture.java:279)
    at com.geckolib.renderer.texture.GeckoLibAnimatedTexture$AnimationInfo.tick(GeckoLibAnimatedTexture.java:245)
    at com.geckolib.renderer.texture.GeckoLibAnimatedTexture.tick(GeckoLibAnimatedTexture.java:175)
    at net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureManager.tick(TextureManager.java:106)
    at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.runTick(Minecraft.java:1200)

It happened every time (3 of 3 attempts, switching en_us -> ru_ru and back). The textures involved are block entity textures with an animated `.mcmeta` that has `"interpolate": true`.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Have a GeckoLib model whose texture has an animation `.mcmeta` with `"interpolate": true` (several frames, e.g. a 6-frame vertical strip, frametime 6).
2. Load a world and look at the model so the texture is loaded.
3. Open Options > Language and switch the language (any reload, e.g. F3+T, should do the same).

**Cause (from reading the source)**
`GeckoLibAnimatedTexture.loadContents` runs on a worker thread during the reload and does:

    if (this.baseImage != null)
        this.baseImage.close();
    this.baseImage = NativeImage.read(stream);

Between `close()` and the assignment the field still points to a closed image, and `animatedTexture` is still the old one. `TextureManager.tick()` keeps ticking the texture on the render thread, so `AnimationInfo.tick()` passes its `baseImage != null` check and `InterpolationData.tickAndUpload` then reads pixels from the closed image. With interpolation this happens on every tick of the reload window, which is why it is easy to hit. The non-interpolated path (`baseImage.copyRect` on a frame change) reads the same field, so it looks exposed too, just far less often.

**Suggested fix**
Read the new image into a local variable, assign it (and the new `AnimationInfo`) first, and close the old image only after that; or make `tick()` skip while a reload of the texture is in progress.

**Side note**
`AnimationInfo.close()` only closes `interpolationData`; `currentFrameBuffer` (a `NativeImage` created in the constructor) is never closed, so each reload leaks it.

issues.title: Reduce per-evaluation allocation in EasingType, keyframe selection and animation hashCodes (1.20.1)
issues.body:
Following the README's request to open an issue before a significant change, here is a proposal I would like to submit as a pull request against `1.20.1`.

1. `EasingType` (4.8.4, branch `1.20.1`) evaluates every easing function through fastutil's boxed `Double2DoubleFunction.apply(Double)` at eight places (`apply(AnimationPoint, Double, double)`, the `easeOut`/`easeInOut` lambdas, the `bounce` combination): each evaluation boxes the input, boxes the result and runs `get(Object)`'s `defaultReturnValue`/`containsKey` checks.
2. `AnimationController.getAnimationPointAtTick` builds a `KeyframeLocation` that its only caller unpacks immediately, and `Keyframe.hashCode`/`RawAnimation.hashCode` go through `Objects.hash` varargs arrays (boxing the keyframe length).
3. Proposed change, source port ready for `1.20.1` (four files under `core/`, no signature changes): a nested `EasingType.PrimitiveEasing extends Double2DoubleFunction` marker implemented by GeckoLib's own lambdas/method references, and a private `evaluate()` that calls `get(double)` for those while custom functions registered by other mods keep the boxed `apply` dispatch they were written against; the keyframe search inlined with the frame and elapsed time in locals; the identical 31-based hashes computed directly.
4. Measured in our pack (Forge 1.20.1, applied to 4.8.4 as a coremod; method-level microbenchmarks, not FPS): mixed easing evaluation 67.35 -> 33.92 ns and 135.76 -> 58.67 B per call; keyframe selection 29.54 -> 25.90 ns and 120 -> 88 B; `Keyframe.hashCode` 18.97 -> 10.47 ns and 80 -> 0 B; `RawAnimation.hashCode` neutral once warm (the JIT already scalar-replaces its array), 80 -> 56 B interpreted.
5. Equivalence: 8,000,000 float comparisons plus the custom-dispatch cases for the easing change, 169,933 keyframe-selection and 233,363 hash comparisons for the others in the coremod form; the source port's 286,376-line regression transcript (every built-in easing type, 40,000 keyframe selections, 80,000 hashes against `Objects.hash`) is byte-identical between the pristine 4.8.4 classes and the classes compiled from this branch (`:core:compileJava :Forge:compileJava` pass).
6. Questions before the PR: is the marker-interface design acceptable (one public nested interface that custom easings may implement to opt in), or would you rather switch every site to `get(double)` outright and accept that a custom `Double2DoubleFunction` overriding the boxed path would change behaviour (much smaller diff)? Should `KeyframeLocation`, unused after the change, be deprecated? Do you want the same change against `main` as well?

Context: these changes ship as configurable switches in Bons and Furious 1.0.15 ([CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/bons-and-furious) · [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/mod/bons-and-furious) · [GitHub 1.0.15 release](https://github.com/BonsUnleashed/bons-and-furious/releases/tag/v1.0.15)); the upstream port keeps GeckoLib's public API unchanged.

issues.title: `[1.21.1] Client crash "IllegalStateException: Not building!" when a glowing GeckoLib entity is hit (stale outline buffer reference)`
issues.body:
**Environment:** Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248, GeckoLib 4.9.2, Mowzie's Mobs 1.8.2 (renderer in the stack, but the mechanism is GeckoLib-generic).

**Reproduction (3/3 on our pack):**
1. Summon a GeckoLib-rendered entity (observed with `mowziesmobs:umvuthi`).
2. Give it the Glowing effect (in the wild, Umvuthi's healers apply it as a game mechanic).
3. Hit the entity (melee or gunfire) while its outline is on screen.
4. Client crashes:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Not building!
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.ensureBuilding(BufferBuilder.java:76)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.addVertex(BufferBuilder.java:156)
  at net.minecraft.client.renderer.OutlineBufferSource$EntityOutlineGenerator.addVertex(OutlineBufferSource.java:58)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexMultiConsumer$Double.addVertex(VertexMultiConsumer.java:79)  (x2)
  at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoRenderer.createVerticesOfQuad(GeoRenderer.java:341)
  at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoRenderer.renderCube(GeoRenderer.java:328)
  at com.bobmowzie.mowziesmobs.client.render.entity.MowzieGeoEntityRenderer.renderRecursively(...)
```

Notably, Glowing **alone does not crash** — we tested a glowing Umvuthana and a glowing vanilla cow standing idle. The crash requires a hit landing while the outline is rendered.

**Mechanism (verified against 1.21.1 bytecode):**

* Vanilla `OutlineBufferSource` backs all glow outlines with **one shared immediate `BufferSource`**; requesting a different `RenderType` from an immediate source **ends the previous builder**.
* `GeoRenderer` fetches the (outline-wrapping) `VertexConsumer` once and holds it across the whole bone pass.
* When the hit lands, something re-enters the same outline source with another render type mid-pass (hurt overlay / held item / a render layer — the exact trigger doesn't change the picture). The shared builder is ended; GeckoLib keeps writing through the stale `EntityOutlineGenerator` reference; the next `addVertex` throws.

**Suggested fix:** re-fetch the buffer from the `MultiBufferSource` whenever the render type can have changed within the bone pass (or per bone/cube batch), instead of holding one `VertexConsumer` across code that may switch render types. Alternatively, catching the ended-builder state before writing would make the outline path tolerant.

**Our modpack-local workaround** (shipped, works): a small client mixin on `EntityOutlineGenerator` that skips writes when the delegate `BufferBuilder` is no longer building — the outline loses one frame instead of crashing the client.

This looks related to older reports of "Not building!" with GeckoLib entities in villages (e.g. irons-spells-n-spellbooks#536, closed as not-their-bug) — same signature, so the root may affect multiple GeckoLib consumers.

Prior art in this tracker: #606 "[1.21] Buffer Builder Not Building! with glowing item/armor render layers on 4.5.7" (closed Aug 2024, "fixed once more in 4.6"). That fix covered the item/armor *layer* path; the trace above is the main bone pass (`GeoRenderer.renderCube → createVerticesOfQuad`) on 4.9.2, so the same stale-outline-buffer situation still exists one level up.

Thanks for the library!

issues.title: Proper Controller Crossfade Support
issues.body:
(Raising this as an issue before any PRs or anything, as agreed upon in the Discord.)

So for Geckolib5, the idea is to essentially just replace the raw additive accumulation with weight-based accumulation for controllers, similar to the way BlockBench does it.

The general idea I had for implementing this (unassuming of any plans you might have to overhaul the system):

- Parse `blendWeight` from animations and store it somewhere.
- Add a `blendWeightMultiplier` in `AnimationController` for finer controller-level manipulation of blend weight.
- Add a getter to `AnimationController` that returns a value based on whether or not it's transitioning. If it has a running animation, it just returns the blend weight from said animation (defaults to `1.0D`). Otherwise, it tries to grab the blend weight of the previous and "current" (upcoming) anim while transitioning and just lerps between them (where any one of them being `null` should default to `0.0D` cuz that represents idle state). Should obv be `0.0D` if the controller itself is idle.
- Run the same render loop BlockBench runs (reset all transforms to 0, grab transforms at current tick from all controllers in a loop, and for each transform from a controller, grab both the weight and "touched" (mutated) bones in said controller's animation and pass those into some separate utility method that keeps track of all transforms and accumulates them). For translations, it's js additive, for rotations, add if we're doing this in Euler angles or multiply the current rot by the conjugate of the default rot for the target bone and normalize to get the relative rotation and slerp using the current weight value (this'll be easier to demonstrate in a code block if we actually proceed dw), and scale is `1.0D + ((curScale.axis() / defScale.axis()) - 1.0D) * weight`.

Again, this is far better demonstrated with some actual code rather than trying to explain it like this, so do let me know if there's anything you would like me to clarify.

issues.title: TextureManagerMixin fails to apply on Forge 1.20.1-47.4.10 (m_118506_ not found) - reproducible on vanilla MDK
issues.body:
**GeckoLib version:** 4.8.3 (also reproduced on 4.7.3)
**Forge version:** 1.20.1-47.4.10 (also reproduced on 47.2.20)
**Mapping:** official, 1.20.1
**Java:** tried both Eclipse Adoptium 17.0.18 and 17.0.20 - same result

### Description
The game crashes on startup (`runClient`) with a Mixin apply failure for
`client.TextureManagerMixin`. The injection target method `m_118506_`
(TextureManager, ResourceLocation -> AbstractTexture) cannot be found.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Download a fresh vanilla Forge MDK for 1.20.1-47.4.10 (no other mods).
2. Add GeckoLib as a dependency in build.gradle:
```groovy
   repositories {
       maven {
           name = 'GeckoLib'
           url 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/geckolib3/geckolib/maven/'
       }
   }
   dependencies {
       implementation fg.deobf("software.bernie.geckolib:geckolib-forge-1.20.1:4.8.3")
   }
```
3. Add the geckolib dependency block to mods.toml.
4. Run `./gradlew runClient`.

This reproduces on a completely untouched MDK with GeckoLib as the ONLY
added dependency (i.e. not specific to any custom mod code).

### Crash log excerpt
[Render thread/FATAL] [mixin/]: Mixin apply failed geckolib.mixins.json:client.TextureManagerMixin -> net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureManager: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InvalidInjectionException Critical injection failure: @Inject annotation on wrapAnimatableTexture could not find any targets matching 'Lnet/minecraft/client/renderer/texture/TextureManager;m_118506_(Lnet/minecraft/resources/ResourceLocation;)Lnet/minecraft/client/renderer/texture/AbstractTexture;' in net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureManager. Using refmap geckolib.refmap.json

### What I've already tried
- Clean rebuild (deleted `.gradle`, `run`, and ForgeGradle global caches)
- Tried GeckoLib 4.8.3 and 4.7.3 (both fail identically) — updated `mods.toml` versionRange accordingly for 4.7.3
- Tried two different JDK 17 builds (Adoptium 17.0.18 / 17.0.20)
- Disabled/excluded antivirus scanning on the project and gradle cache folders, then fully disabled the antivirus (including AMSI protection) and deleted/re-downloaded the GeckoLib deobf cache — same exact crash still occurs
- Confirmed the issue also occurs on a brand-new, completely vanilla MDK with GeckoLib as the only dependency (rules out any custom mod code as the cause)
- Tried an older Forge patch, **47.2.20**, on the same vanilla MDK + GeckoLib 4.8.3 setup — same exact crash occurs, ruling out a specific Forge patch version as the cause
- Tried pinning the ForgeGradle plugin version explicitly (the range `[6.0,6.2)` was resolving to `6.0.54`) down to `6.0.24` — same exact crash still occurs

### Important note: works fine as a player

issues.title: GeckoLib 5.5.1 silently treats camelCase easing names as linear due to case-sensitive easing lookup
issues.body:
### Version
GeckoLib 5.5.1

### Summary
Animation keyframes using common camelCase easing names such as `easeInOutSine`, `easeOutSine`, or `easeInCubic` are silently resolved as `linear`.

This appears to happen because GeckoLib registers built-in easing names in lowercase, but the animation JSON loader passes the raw easing string into the lookup without normalizing case.

### Actual behavior
When an animation JSON contains:

```json
{
  "easing": "easeInOutSine"
}
```

the easing does not behave as easeInOutSine. It falls back to linear interpolation with no warning or error.

### Expected behavior

GeckoLib should either:

- Accept easing names case-insensitively, or
- Emit a warning/error when an easing name is unknown

At the moment it silently degrades to linear, which makes easing failures hard to diagnose.

### Root cause

From source inspection in GeckoLib 5.5.1:

ActorBoneAnimationKeyframe uses the raw JSON string directly:

EasingType.fromString(this.interpolationType)
EasingType registers built-in names in lowercase only, for example:

- easeinoutsine
- easeoutsine
- easeincubic

EasingType.fromString(String name) performs a case-sensitive map lookup and falls back to EasingType.LINEAR if no match is found.

So values like easeInOutSine do not match easeinoutsine, and the animation silently becomes linear.

### Suggested fix
Normalize easing names before lookup, for example:
```
EasingType.fromString(this.interpolationType.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT))
```

or make `EasingType.fromString` itself case-insensitive.

It would also help to log a warning when an easing name is unknown instead of silently defaulting to linear.

issues.title: Animation time appears quantized to 0.5-tick on non-Entity renderers (MC 26.1.2)
issues.body:
## Body

Hi GeckoLib team — thanks for maintaining this, it's been a huge help on our project.

While debugging a "low-FPS-looking" animation at 200+ render FPS on a custom `GeoItemRenderer`, we think we traced it to how `DataTickets.TICK` is populated on non-Entity render states. Posting in case it's unintentional or worth a look; happy to close if it's by design.

### Environment

- GeckoLib 26.1.2
- Minecraft 26.1.2 (Fabric)
- Custom `GeoItemRenderer` subclass (the same pattern also reproduces on a `GeoObjectRenderer`)

### Observed behavior

On a plain `GeoRenderState` (Item / ObjectRenderer path — anything that doesn't land on `EntityRenderStateMixin.getAnimatableAge`), `renderState.getAnimatableAge()` advances in 0.5-tick steps (e.g. `…963.5, 963.5, 964.0, 964.0, 964.0, 964.5, …`) even at 200 render FPS.

The `partialTick` parameter passed into `addRenderData(..., float partialTick)` is frame-smooth in the same frames (multiple distinct values per tick, matching `DeltaTracker.getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick(false)` when sampled right there).

Downstream effect: `AnimationController.checkControllerState` computes `timeDelta` from `getAnimatableAge()` → `timelineTime`, `animationPoint.animTime` all step at 0.025s → bone output quantizes to ~40 Hz regardless of render FPS, making all animations look choppy.

### Suspected cause: inconsistent `ignoreFrozenGame` flag

`GeoRendererInternals.captureDefaultRenderState` (L83–84):

```java
if (!DataTickets.TICK.canExtractFrom(renderState))
    renderState.addGeckolibData(DataTickets.TICK, ClientUtil.getCurrentTick());
```

`ClientUtil.getCurrentTick()` (L53–59):

```java
return mc.level != null ?
    mc.level.getGameTime() + mc.getDeltaTracker().getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick(false) :
    Blaze3D.getTime() * 20d;
```

Meanwhile, `GeckolibItemSpecialRenderer.buildRenderState` (L81–82) calls `fillRenderState` with:

```java
Minecraft.getInstance().getDeltaTracker().getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick(true)
```

So within a single `fillRenderState` call chain:
- `DataTickets.PARTIAL_TICK` ends up storing the `ignoreFrozenGame=true` value (the `partialTick` parameter)
- `DataTickets.TICK` is built from the `ignoreFrozenGame=false` value (via `ClientUtil.getCurrentTick()`)

Per `DeltaTracker.Timer.getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick` (MC 26.1.2):

```java
public float getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick(final boolean ignoreFrozenGame) {
    if (ignoreFrozenGame || !this.frozen) {
        return this.paused ? this.pausedDeltaTickResidual : this.deltaTickResidual;
    }
    return 1.0f;
}
```

In contexts where `frozen` (or some related state) is true, `(true)` returns the smooth residual while `(false)` returns `1.0f`, so `DataTickets.PARTIAL_TICK` and `DataTickets.TICK` end up derived from different values. In our test scenario we observed `DataTickets.TICK` stepping at 0.5-tick granularity while `DataTickets.PARTIAL_TICK` stayed frame-smooth in the same frames — consistent with the two sources diverging, though we didn't fully identify which MC state was triggering it (possibly pause-related, or tied to the new 1.21 extract/render split).

Entity renderers are not affected, because `EntityRenderStateMixin` overrides `getAnimatableAge()` to read `state.ageInTicks`, which vanilla fills with a render-smooth value regardless of this flag.

### Workaround we're using

In our Item renderer's `addRenderData` we overwrite TICK using the `partialTick` parameter:

```java
if (level != null) {
    renderState.addGeckolibData(DataTickets.TICK, level.getGameTime() + partialTick);
}
```

For our 3p `GeoObjectRenderer` we use the `AvatarRenderState.ageInTicks` value as the TICK source instead (since it's rendered from a `LivingEntityRenderer.submit` override and that field is already render-smooth from vanilla).

Both fully resolve the symptom on our end.

### Possible directions (just suggestions)

1. Have `captureDefaultRenderState` use the `partialTick` parameter directly when computing TICK (something like `mc.level.getGameTime() + partialTick`), skipping the internal `ClientUtil.getCurrentTick()` call. This keeps `TICK` and `PARTIAL_TICK` consistent with each other since both derive from the same caller-supplied value.
2. Or align the flags — pick one of `(true)` or `(false)` for both read sites and document it. This would also resolve the inconsistency.

The `Blaze3D.getTime() * 20d` fallback for when `mc.level == null` can stay intact either way.

### Reproduction

Any non-Entity Geo animatable at >50 render FPS, with a keyframe animation. Log `renderState.getAnimatableAge()` or `controller.getCurrentAnimationTime()` each predicate call; you should see 0.025s step progression rather than frame-smooth.

---

Full disclosure: I worked through this with an AI assistant (Claude) to navigate the source. The log traces, the symptom, and the workaround were verified on our end. That said, my read of Minecraft's `DeltaTracker` internals may be wrong — the "suspected cause" paragraph is my best guess based on what the logs show, not a confirmed claim. Please verify independently before acting on it. Raw logs / more repro detail available if useful. Thanks for looking.

issues.title: Sound keyframes can be skipped because sound_effects are not kept in timestamp order
issues.body:
Using GeckoLib 5.5 on Minecraft 26.1, I found that some animation sound keyframes are skipped even though the animation timeline passes through their timestamps.

**Steps to reproduce**
Use an animation with multiple sound_effects, for example:
```
"sound_effects": {
  "0.0": { "effect": "inspect_up" },
  "0.5333": { "effect": "m4_unloadnew" },
  "0.8833": { "effect": "m4_reloadnew" },
  "1.3667": { "effect": "inspect_down" }
}
```

Play the animation and log sound keyframe callbacks.

**Actual behavior**
Only some sound markers fire. In my repro, 0.0 and 1.3667 fired, but 0.5333 and 0.8833 were skipped, even though the animation time advanced past them.

**Expected behavior**
All sound markers should fire once their timestamps are crossed.

**Likely cause**
JsonUtil.jsonObjToMap(...) stores sound_effects in Object2ObjectOpenHashMap, which does not preserve order, while AnimationTimeline.getKeyframesForAnimation(...) assumes markers are sorted and does an early break when marker.getTime() > endTime.

**Workaround / fix**
Sorting keyframe markers by timestamp before scanning them fixes the issue.

issues.title: NullPointerException in GeoArmorRenderer when checking entity glow status
issues.body:
## Bug Report: NullPointerException in GeoArmorRenderer when checking entity glow status

### Description
Game crashes when rendering armor on entities due to a null entity being passed to `shouldEntityAppearGlowing()` method in `GeoArmorRenderer.java` line 333.

### Minecraft Version
- **Minecraft**: 1.21.1
- **NeoForge**: 21.1.216
- **GeckoLib**: 4.8.2 (geckolib-neoforge-1.21.1-4.8.2.jar)

### Crash Location
```
at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoArmorRenderer.renderToBuffer(GeoArmorRenderer.java:333)
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.shouldEntityAppearGlowing(Minecraft.java:2609)
```

### Root Cause
The `GeoArmorRenderer.renderToBuffer()` method at line 333 calls `Minecraft.getInstance().shouldEntityAppearGlowing(entity)` without checking if the entity parameter is null first.

### Error Message
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity.isCurrentlyGlowing()" because "p_91315_" is null
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Join a multiplayer server with GeckoLib-based armor mods installed
2. Navigate to the Nether dimension
3. Encounter Zombified Piglins wearing modded armor
4. Game crashes when trying to render the entity

### Affected Entities
- Zombified Piglins (minecraft:zombified_piglin)
- Likely affects any mob wearing GeckoLib-based armor

### Mods Involved
- **Immersive Armors** 1.7.5
- **Advanced Netherite** 2.3.1
- **Ars Nouveau** 5.10.6 (uses entity lighting system)
- **Accessories** mod (involved in armor rendering pipeline)

### Expected Behavior
The renderer should gracefully handle null entities without crashing.

### Suggested Fix
Add a null check in `GeoArmorRenderer.renderToBuffer()` before calling glow methods:
```java
// Line 333 in GeoArmorRenderer.java
if (entity != null && Minecraft.getInstance().shouldEntityAppearGlowing(entity)) {
    // ... glow rendering code
}
```

### Additional Context
- Crash occurs consistently at specific coordinates in the Nether
- Happens during armor layer rendering (`HumanoidArmorLayer.render`)
- The crash persists even after disabling dynamic lighting features in client mods
- Multiple other mods are applying mixins to the armor rendering pipeline (Accessories, Iris, etc.)

### Environment
- **OS**: Windows 11
- **Java**: OpenJDK 21.0.9
- **Graphics**: AMD Radeon RX 7600
- **Total Mods**: 375+ installed

### Workarounds Attempted
- ✗ Disabling Iron's Spellbooks glow features
- ✗ Disabling Ars Nouveau entity lights
- ✗ Adjusting client rendering configs
- ✗ The crash persists in all cases

### Priority
**HIGH** - This is a critical crash that prevents gameplay in the Nether dimension with any GeckoLib armor installed.

issues.title: [Bug] Looped Animations Aren't Looping on v5.4
issues.body:
RawAnimations which are marked as looped(via `RawAnimation.begin().thenLoop(<animName>)`) aren't being looped if the Animation Controller's transition ticks are greater than 0.

If the transition ticks are greater than 0, they'll play once before stopping all animations. If the transition ticks is less than or equal to 0, the looping works as expected(I'm unsure if negative transition ticks are intended or not).

Looping animations did work as expected in 5.4-alpha-1.

Info:
- Minecraft 1.21.11
- Fabric 0.18.3 (NeoForge/Forge untested)
- GeckoLib 5.4
- My mod's repo with my entities can be linked if wanted.

Extra Info:
I believe the issue comes from this commit, 82644b33a516726484fd61dd98d34fc516458c33 , which added an extra transition AnimationTimeline.Stage as the final Stage.

That then messes with the `MiscUtil.areFloatsEqual` check at [AnimationController#L580](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/main/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/animation/AnimationController.java#L580), because the `timelineTime` has been clamped to the new transition Stage(which is now the final Stage) end time via [AnimationController#L512](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/main/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/animation/AnimationController.java#L512), which is now higher than the `currentAnimStage.endTime()` used in the floats check.

The `currentAnimStage` via [AnimationTimeline#getAnimationStage](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/main/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/animation/state/AnimationTimeline.java#L84) gets the current stage if it isn't a transition, the next stage if current isn't last, or the second-last stage if current is the last stage. 

Because the last Stage in the AnimationTimeline is now a transition, getAnimationStage returns the second-last stage, whose end time doesn't equal the last stage's end time being used to clamp the timelineTime. The floats check in the AnimationController then never returns true, which prevents the animationPoint's LoopType(in this case, LoopType.LOOP) from [updating the timelineTime](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/main/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/animation/object/LoopType.java#L35) via [AnimationController#L581](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/main/common/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/animation/AnimationController.java#L581), preventing the `LoopType.LOOP` from working.

Seemingly prior to this commit(e.g. in 5.4-alpha-1), the last Stage in the AnimationTimeline would be normal animation Stage, and it would have the correct end time being used to clamp the timelineTime.

I have not confirmed my theory by undoing the commit's additions, as I don't have the repo cloned yet and couldn't figure out how to do it via mixins. I'm also not familiar enough with the specifics beyond this to feel comfortable suggesting a fix(assuming my theory is right), as I don't know how to fix both the issue the commit intended to fix and this without possible extra side effects. But hopefully this at least helps a little.

This issue was reported to me on NeoForge 1.21.1, but it may be on newer versions too I don't have the time to check currently
PAL mixins into the `setPartVisibility` method of the `HumanoidArmorLayer` class to set some of the parts to be no longer be visible
This seems to work just fine for every piece of armor other than the leggings
https://github.com/ZigyTheBird/PlayerAnimationLibrary/issues/67#issuecomment-3650663971

issues.title: Blockbench plugin keeps forgetting the model type
issues.body:
The plugin fails to persist the model type leading to the model always being loaded with the `entity` type model even though it was saved as an `item` type for example.

Blockbench v5.0.4
Geckolib Plugin v4.2.2

issues.title: Blockbench Plugin ignores/resets mirrored display slot settings
issues.body:
The blockbench plugin doesn't respect display settings with negative scale (i.e. Allowing Display Slot Mirroring in the settings). 
Exporting the display settings or saving the project both do not preserve the negative scale.

Blockbench v5.0.4
Geckolib Plugin v4.2.2

issues.title: Geckolib mods ignore CPM armor settings
issues.body: The title says it all. Any mods that use Geckolib for rendering armor seem to ignore Customizable Player Models. My model has all armor disabled in CPM settings since the character has his own set of armor that he is wearing in the image, but the helmet is still being rendered.

issues.title: Bugged head bone transformations
issues.body:
**Hi!** 👋

I have a capybara entity with a walking animation. I also override the head bone so it turns in the direction the capybara looks. When this override exists and there are several capybaras on screen and at least one of them is walking, the head moves on all of them (the head is part of the walking animation).

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Create a mob model and a walking animation for it that affects the head.
2. In the mob model code, set the head bone to rotate toward a look target or use `DefaultedEntityGeoModel`.
3. Spawn several mobs. When one of them walks within view, look at another one that is currently idle. The idle mob will start moving its head as if the walking animation is playing only for the head bone.

_Minecraft 1.21.1, Neoforge 21.1.215, Geckolib 4.8.2_

**Entity:** https://github.com/Octo-Studios/re-animal/blob/master/src/main/java/it/hurts/shatterbyte/reanimal/world/entity/capybara/CapybaraEntity.java
**Model:** https://github.com/Octo-Studios/re-animal/blob/master/src/main/java/it/hurts/shatterbyte/reanimal/client/model/capybara/CapybaraModel.java

issues.title: In Blockbench 5.0, UV cannot be rotated in Per-Face UV mode on a GeckoLib model.
issues.body:
In Blockbench 5.0, when using the GeckoLib Models and Animations plugin and editing a GeckoLib animated model with Per-Face UV, the slider to change a UV face's rotation is missing. 
When added to the toolbar manually it still does not appear. It is greyed out, with the text under stating _"Some tools might be hidden because they are not available in the current mode, format, or situation."_ 

Models which had faces rotated like this still have the rotation applied, so it would seem the format still supports UV rotation, but is communicating to Blockbench that it does not, or not communicating that it does.

issues.title: Step type easing is limited to 2 steps at minimum
issues.body:
Hiya~
We're using your plugin for our game Tesera (thank you by the way, you made an awesome job saving us a lot of nerve cells) and I'm curently working on blinking animation. I noticed that Step type easing doesn't work as expected when I want to make an instant transition from one keyframe to another one.
Since I can't set 1 step for this type, I thought that it just counts both positions (initial and final)
But it actually makes an additional frame between these two.
So my question is why this was made. I even see this strict error in the code
```
if (steps < 2)
        throw new Error("steps must be > 2, got:" + steps);
```
So it was made intentionally.

Also changing steps count manually directly in the file gives me the exact expected behaviour in our game without additional frame. So it actually works like it should?

As a reference we're using this tool where 1 step is a valid option as well
https://animejs.com/easing-editor/steps/start

issues.title: [Suggestion] Pass along partialTick to GeoRenderer#addRenderData
issues.body: The partialTicks which would be useful for interpolating custom RenderData are already present in `GeoRenderer#fillRenderState`, they just need to be passed as a parameter to `GeoRenderer#addRenderData`.

issues.title: [1.20.1] Replaced entities' custom animations aren't interpolated
issues.body:
On 1.20.1, any replaced entity that has custom animations (referring to `setCustomAnimations` that handles animating programatically rather than via Blockbench or related) will have a very noticeable jitter, likely due to the values not getting interpolated?
It's pretty easy to notice when you look at the head rotations being weirdly jittery compared to the non-replaced entities.

issues.title: Bug: Cannot register GeckoLib GeoEntityRenderer with EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers on NeoForge
issues.body:
❓ What I'm Trying To Do

I'm creating a custom entity (ForesterEntity) using NeoForge 1.21.4 / version 21.4.137, and using GeckoLib 4.7 for NeoForge 1.21.1 to add animations.

I created a custom renderer:

public class ForesterRenderer extends GeoEntityRenderer<ForesterEntity> { ... }

Then I attempted to register it via EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers like so:

event.registerEntityRenderer(ModEntities.FORESTER.get(), ForesterRenderer::new);

Or with explicit casting:

event.registerEntityRenderer(ModEntities.FORESTER.get(),
    (EntityRendererProvider<ForesterEntity>) (context -> new ForesterRenderer(context)));

💥 The Error

I consistently get this compile-time error:

error: incompatible types: bad return type in method reference
ForesterRenderer cannot be converted to EntityRenderer<ForesterEntity,?>

Even though:

    ForesterRenderer extends GeoEntityRenderer<ForesterEntity>

    GeoEntityRenderer<T> implements EntityRenderer<T>

✅ What I’ve Tried

    Lambda syntax with cast

    Triple-casting to raw types

    Wrapper/bridge class returning new ForesterRenderer(context)

    Suppressing warnings

    Registering during RegisterRenderers and client setup

    Confirmed that the method signature of ForesterRenderer matches expected EntityRendererProvider<ForesterEntity>

📦 Versions

    NeoForge: 21.4.137 (for Minecraft 1.21.4)

    GeckoLib: 4.7 for NeoForge 1.21.1

    Java: Java 21

    Gradle: 8.5+

🧩 Suspected Issue

It appears there’s a type erasure or generic mismatch between:

    NeoForge’s EntityRendererProvider<T>

    GeckoLib’s GeoEntityRenderer<T> (which does implement EntityRenderer<T>)

This might be caused by NeoForge being overly strict in its generic inference or due to GeckoLib’s generic signature using additional type parameters internally.
✅ What I'm Hoping For

    A way to cleanly register a GeoEntityRenderer<T> as an EntityRendererProvider<T>

    Or clarification on how GeckoLib renderers are expected to be registered under NeoForge 1.21.4

issues.title: [1.20.1] v4.71 breaks `AbstractContainerMenu` slot listener implementation due to faulty Mixin code
issues.body:
This is causing problems like this one: https://github.com/Fuzss/easyanvils/issues/96

The issue lies here: https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/be8fe53d7bcd3b296bffb8bd98e952d378347761/Forge/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/mixin/common/AbstractContainerMenuMixin.java#L33

This should be:
```java
    public boolean geckolib$forceGeckolibIdSync(ItemStack stack, ItemStack other) {
        return ItemStack.matches(stack, other) &&
               (!stack.hasTag() || !stack.getTag().contains(GeoItem.ID_NBT_KEY) ||
               !other.hasTag() || !other.getTag().contains(GeoItem.ID_NBT_KEY) ||
               stack.getTag().get(GeoItem.ID_NBT_KEY).equals(other.getTag().get(GeoItem.ID_NBT_KEY)));
    }
```

Also goes for the other method in the class.

issues.title: Add Cube requirements for ItemArmorGeoLayer to Wiki
issues.body:
Currently, the wiki doesn't give any specifics for how the ItemArmorGeoLayer needs to be set up in the model of the entity it is being added to. The assumptions for this render layer require the armor bones to have a single cube the shape and size of where you want that armor piece to be. If no cubes are included, the layer will crash. If multiple are added, only the first will be used.

Since this is the standard usage of a library-supplied render layer, details for usage should be easily documented.

Instead, a `Logger` should be use so that
1. it identifies the source of the log message
2. it properly indicates that it is a warning/error
3. it prints a newline at the end of the message, avoiding these very long lines

If, for whatever reason, it is not possible to use a logger, then consider at the very least doing one of the following:
1. ```java
   System.out.printf("Could not load animation: %s. Is it missing?%n", rawAnimation.animationName);
   ```
   (note: the `%n` at the end of the message)
2. ```java
   System.out.println("Could not load animation: " + rawAnimation.animationName + ". Is it missing?");
   ```

Even if 3.x versions are no longer maintained, this is a rather small release so it does not require a lot of effort to do.

Normally, the animatable is set in `GeoArmorRenderer#prepForRender`, then reset to null, but it appears this is bypassed when vanilla attempts to render enchantment glint or trims (simply putting a geo item in the smithing table causes this) because vanilla directly calls to `GeoArmorRenderer#renderToBuffer`. Therefore the current `animatable` is still null.

https://gist.github.com/TomatoSoupter/049d5565843d2d5c1bfe9f28d9eab039
https://gist.github.com/iron431/32dec18da4952771044222d7ce8dd113

issues.title: Off-screen animations play from the start once the animating entity is rendered, regardless of timing
issues.body:
If an animation starts while a mob is not rendered, the animation will play from the beginning. Instead, the animation should play as though it had started already, taking into account the time spent not rendered. If the animation's full duration had passed while not rendered, the animation should not play at all.

This gremlin example plays an interact animation when given an item. However, if the player looks away before the animation begins, the animation won't play until the player looks back at the Gremlin. Not very consequential for an interact animation, but for an attack animation that players need to dodge or block with correct timing, this would make a big difference.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00a109ec-a852-40b5-8386-951fb5c0da19

issues.title: [1.20.1] Entity model has incorrect lighting (Geckolib 4.4.2)
issues.body:
In in-game rendering, when lighting is applied to a model, it seems to ignore the rotation angles of its groups or bones.

1.The model I created in Blockbench is like this: place the "cube" bone in the "Base" group and rotate them 90 degrees around the Z-axis
![a](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/73044568/39ddc6c7-e629-4a4b-944e-b2074ba99f7d)
2.The "cube" bone looks like this when not setting a rotation angle for its group.
![b](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/73044568/ca9a1839-6d27-4c23-b6c4-f35de919e5c5)
3.When I imported it as a Entity model into the game, the lighting of the model seemed to be abnormal.
The lighting in the game did not seem to set shadows in the direction of the final rotation, but ignored the rotation of the group and bones, only giving lighting in the "cube" state without rotation.
![c](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/73044568/f16621bc-4f4f-497f-bd86-258d75eb3309)
The shadow I am looking forward to should be like Figure 1, with the green side being the directly illuminated side.  
I'm not sure if this is an issue with GeckoLib or a rendering issue with version 1.20.1.
The above model is just an example, in fact, my model has many bones or groups that have undergone many rotations, which results in different parts of the model having bad shadows in the game.

issues.title: Geckolib 4.5 fails to resolve some math expressions that older Geckolib versions could resolve
issues.body:
If you try to add some "offset" for either sin or cos functions, this will result in Geckolib not resolving those functions correctly (or preventing querys from working correctly, idk what is exactly happening here). Like:
`25+math.sin(query.anim_time*360/4-90)*3` - being passed as angle, this will result in bone being constantly angled at 25 degrees on axis where this expression was put and it will not change over time despite the query. Similar result also happens if you try to add value rather than substract, or use such expression for changing bone position or scaling
`25+math.sin(query.anim_time*360/4)*3` - this will work and change over time just fine

Some videos with demonstration of the bug:
- MC version 1.20.6, Geckolib 4.5.1: https://youtu.be/sSW8BL7_2o4
- MC version 1.20.4, Geckolib 4.4.4: https://youtu.be/mmWuiEUmcyI

Exact same model, exact same animation files. In Blockbench animation matches the one shown in video with Geckolib 4.4.4

Link to repos of the mod with links relevant files:
- 1.20.6, Geckolib 4.5.1:
- - Repo: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/tree/1.20.6
- - Animation file: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/blob/1.20.6/src/main/resources/assets/uselessreptile/animations/entity/lightning_chaser/lightning_chaser.animation.json
- - Model file: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/blob/1.20.6/src/main/resources/assets/uselessreptile/geo/entity/lightning_chaser/lightning_chaser.geo.json
- - Entity class: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/blob/1.20.6/src/main/java/nordmods/uselessreptile/common/entity/LightningChaserEntity.java

- 1.20.4, Geckolib 4.4.4:
- - Repo: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/tree/1.20.4
- - Animation file: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/blob/1.20.4/src/main/resources/assets/uselessreptile/animations/entity/lightning_chaser/lightning_chaser.animation.json
- - Model file: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/blob/1.20.4/src/main/resources/assets/uselessreptile/geo/entity/lightning_chaser/lightning_chaser.geo.json
- - Entity class: https://github.com/NordAct/useless-reptile/blob/1.20.4/src/main/java/nordmods/uselessreptile/common/entity/LightningChaserEntity.java

issues.title: Client stalls on startup & resourcepack load/reload when loading a model with missing parent bones
issues.body:
### GeckoLib Version
geckolib-forge-1.20.1-4.4.4

## Bug Description
The client stalls on startup or resourcepack load/reload when geckolib tries to load model geometry with **bones that reference a non-existing parent bone**.

Profiling has shown that `GeometryTree.fromModel()` is the culprit for the stalling.
https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/c6a809c18a080defe1d74028c73d7ca4eafa3881/Forge/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/loading/object/GeometryTree.java#L17

### Expected Behavior
The client should crash or skip loading of the faulty model.

### How to replicate
Place the following model into your `assets/<namespace>/geo` folder or use this resourcepack [geckolib_bug.zip](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/files/14723805/geckolib_bug.zip)

```json
{
	"format_version": "1.12.0",
	"minecraft:geometry": [
		{
			"description": {
				"identifier": "geometry.unknown",
				"texture_width": 16,
				"texture_height": 16,
				"visible_bounds_width": 2,
				"visible_bounds_height": 1.5,
				"visible_bounds_offset": [0, 0.25, 0]
			},
			"bones": [
				{
					"name": "orphan",
					"parent": "missing_parent",
					"pivot": [0, 0, 0],
					"cubes": [
						{"origin": [-1, 0, -1], "size": [2, 2, 2], "uv": [0, 0]}
					]
				}
			]
		}
	]
}
```

>[!important] 
> The bone "orphan" is referencing the **non-existing** parent bone "missing_parent"

## How to easily produce faulty models with Blockbench

![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/6061273/d64963a8-c3b4-47cf-bf45-f4b87e6d542b)

>[!important] 
> Please take note of how i disabled the export of the parent bone

issues.title: Crashing when rendering: "Cannot read field "bone" because "snapshot" is null"
issues.body:
Hi there,
I've had this issue happen multiple times with a few different mods that both use GeckoLib; once with Plenty of Golems and once with Enderman Overhaul. It evidently happens when rendering specific entities.
When the game tries to render these entities in some worlds/scenarios, the screen freezes, then turns white, then the game crashes.
I can render these mobs fine in other worlds (like in a Superflat testing world) and I've rendered them fine before, but in some scenarios it'll completely crash the game, bricking entire worlds.

I've attached two crash logs that both point to GeckoLib as the problem. They both have the same error message:
`java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read field "bone" because "snapshot" is null`

[crash-2024-03-17_15.41.09-client.txt](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/files/14626398/crash-2024-03-17_15.41.09-client.txt)
[crash-2024-03-17_16.14.08-client.txt](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/files/14626399/crash-2024-03-17_16.14.08-client.txt)

In a different thread that was also seeing NullPointerExceptions you recommended to remove EntityCulling, I did this and the issue still persists. Is there other mods that would affect this?

Please help, this is driving me crazy and making my worlds unplayable!

issues.title: Regarding Fabric-NeoForge Versions
issues.body:
As a lot of players do, I play with the new bridge between Forge and Fabric, Synitra Connector. When trying to use Gecko dependent mods, the easy solution is to use Fabric Gecko and let Sinytra convert it to a compat one with Forge Gecko... or that's how it should work. 
One flaw for this was the famous mod, Ars Nouveau, which has built-in forge gecko, so when trying to use it alongside Fabric gecko, wouldn't work. With Ars Nouveau team help, I made a jar that does not have the forge gecko, and added the fabric one manually.
When using the fabric one, the game starts up properly and even loads the world, but crashes when trying to render items (for example, the spell book) it didn't crashed just for entities (for example, dragmys from the same mod).
I reported the issue both to Ars Nouveau team and Sinytra team, and the lates recomended me notifying you as it seams to be a disparity between Fabric and Forge gecko. 
I did two different tests, the first one (https://pastebin.com/7CG3Whc3) was with the previous version when it crashed with item rendering, the second (https://pastebin.com/DvH9vatm) with the newest one that crashes with entity rendering.
I thank your team as it has helped doing awesome mods as a useful library, and maybe working this alongside Connector team may also help the whole community to be more unite. 
Thanks for checking.

issues.title: [1.20.1] AutoGlowingGeoLayer on armor shows up completely black
Geckolib Example Mod Crashes My Data Generator.
issues.body:
I'm working on a mod integration addon for Dragon Survival and Spectrum. As the former is Forge-only and the latter is Fabric-only, this addon depends on Sinytra Connector. The addon does not itself require Geckolib, but Dragon Survival does. Somehow, the combination of Geckolib's Example Mod, Additional Entity Attributes (a dependency of Spectrum), and Sinytra Connector causes my runData configuration to crash with the following log: [latest.log](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/files/14530305/latest.log)

Would it be possible to add a way to disable the Geckolib Example Mod in a workspace where it isn't needed (or if there's already a way to do this, add it to the documentation?), or provide a maven artifact that doesn't include it? I've spent a few hours already trying to fix this issue on my end and have yet to find a solution.

issues.title: Shader Armor Reflections incompatible
issues.body:
When using Iris shaders supporting labPBR resource packs, armor reflections are not present.

Active mods:
- GeckoLib 4.2.4
- Iris
- QFAPI
- Sodium

To replicate, use any shader with labPBR resource pack support, e.g. [Complementary Reimagined](https://modrinth.com/shader/complementary-reimagined), and a resource pack with PBR formatted textures, e.g. [DefaultPBR](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/defaultpbr). (Modrinth links)

issues.title: creeper.png forces mipmap level of 3 due to non-16x height
issues.body:
Hi, I noticed that from a mod shoving everything into the block atlas, the creeper.png file provided by geckolib is forcing the mipmap level to 3 instead of 4 due to the height of 40.

### The file:
https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/1.20.1/Fabric/src/main/resources/assets/geckolib/textures/entity/creeper.png

From F3+S dump: `geckolib:entity/creeper	x=1408	y=2000	w=64	h=40`

### Possible fixes:
Align the creeper to the nearest power of 2 or multiple of 16 that can still fit the atlas, which would be 64 and 48 respectively.

This would allow any mod that for any reason takes the creeper and other entities and throws it into a bigger atlas to work seamlessly.

issues.title: GeckoLib3 has failed to load correctly
Broken Mob Animations When Using Geckolib Mods with Iris Shaders
issues.body:
I found this same issue in a previously closed (and supposedly fixed) post from a previous version, but it's still a thing.
Basically any mod with geckolib dependencies will have animation bugs, when using Iris shaders *with* Entity Shadows enabled. Mobs are still able to move around, but their animations are frozen or erratic, no idle animations, no moving legs, etc. Turning off Entity Shadows fixes the animations again.

When only one (geckolib modded) mob is in frame, sometimes the animations work properly even with Entity Shadows enabled, but as soon as you spawn a second mob next to it, the first one freezes and the only the second one has proper animations.

In my tests I was using Forge 1.20.1, Iris Shaders 1.6.10, BSL Shaders 8.2.06, Creeper Overhaul 3.0.1 and Geckolib 4.2.3

issues.title: [1.20.1] Armor Render bug with Iris shaders
issues.body:
**Minecraft version** - 1.20.1
**Mod loader** - Fabric 0.14.22
**Mod version** - geckolib-fabric-1.20.1-4.2.2

The issue is present on 1.20.1 at least since Sodium 0.5.0 + Iris 1.6.5.

**Describe the bug**
When using any Iris shader, GeckoLib re-renders the Gecko armor worn by the client player in the distance.
![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/4989469/003a03a2-597a-4f43-a4fc-ce8fb3797a4c)
![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/4989469/661d8540-010f-46d2-bd7b-47d7b3ccd238)
![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/4989469/1e884ed0-3b1a-49cb-a3d7-f3a54607a51b)

https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/4989469/cec8a9d4-1806-4d3d-a373-3405b10ba8c3

This issue does not occur when wearing armor sets with vanilla armor model.

**To Reproduce**
1. Install any mod (and all of its dependencies) that uses GeckoLib Armor Renderer featurset AND the latest version of Sodium and Iris. (In this example I install my own mod: Wizards and all of its depencies.)
2. Install Sodium 0.5.2 and Iris 1.6.8
3. Install any shaderpack (for example Complementary Shaders)
4. Enter the game, equip a Gecko rendered armor set
5. Look at the sky

The full modlist that was used to reproduce this scenario:
- cloth-config-11.1.106-fabric.jar
- fabric-api-0.87.0+1.20.1.jar
- geckolib-fabric-1.20.1-4.2.2.jar
- iris-mc1.20.1-1.6.8.jar
- player-animation-lib-fabric-1.0.2-rc1+1.20.jar
- runes-fabric-0.9.10+1.20.1.jar
- sodium-fabric-mc1.20.1-0.5.2.jar
- spell_engine-fabric-0.9.29+1.20.1.jar
- spell_power-fabric-0.9.15+1.20.1.jar
- trinkets-3.7.1.jar
- wizards-fabric-0.9.20+1.20.1.jar

Note: This modlist is long due to how many dependencies Wizards has, any mod that is using GeckoLib armor renderer can reproduce this alongside Iris shaders.

**Expected behavior**
Worn armor rendered on the actual player model only, nowhere else in the viewport.

issues.title: Geo armor rendering using the ItemArmorLayer is broken
issues.body:
The armor is not scaled and aligned correctly on the entity.

Interestingly, the moment the armor gets rendered at least once on a non-geckolib entity (i.e. using the vanilla armor layer), the position and scaling fixes itself.

https://streamable.com/jk5uxy

This applies to every armor registered *individually*. 

So if i equip the lizard example armor on the gremlin, it will appear misaligned, then i equip the armor (any piece) on a armor stand. Then the armor is fixed on the gremlin.

Now, if we equip the wolf armor on the gremlin, it will be misaligned, until any piece is rendered on a player, zombie, skeleton, armor stand etc.

issues.title: MixinItemRenderer on fabric is not working properly
issues.body:
MixinItemRenderer targets `render` at `renderByItem`: 
![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/60247969/cffca0c5-c94b-4770-b010-1c9632dc3ee3)
It calls [`RenderProvider.of(stack).getCustomRenderer().renderByItem(...)`](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/24446090754686c674b28b983cbc5d1b128f7d08/Fabric/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib/mixins/fabric/MixinItemRenderer.java#L22), and nothing else.
Looking at the code, this seems to just call the vanilla BEWLR a second time:
- `RenderProvider.of` returns DEFAULT for a non-geo item
- DEFAULT returns MC's BEWLR
- calls `renderByItem` on the returned BEWLR

The original call is not canceled, so both happen.

There's two problems here:
- geo items go through custom rendering *and* vanilla rendering
- non-geo items rendered via BEWLR are always rendered twice

For most items, this is not an issue (besides lag), but for some custom ones, it is:
![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/60247969/edb21e34-3a3a-4bef-8245-734c7fa1cbe2)

issues.title: [1.20.1] Lighting is baked incorrectly for rotated item models
issues.body:
Sword model from 1.19, geckolib 3 with correct lighting:
![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/13970203/3f36bc3a-6945-40eb-8029-17eeaf38dcbb)

1.20.1/geckolib 4
Item models with incorrect lighting. The book with rotated (2nd), book without rotations and correct lighting (third) sword with incorrect lighting, unchanged from 1.19/g3 (4th)

![image](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/assets/13970203/33838ce3-0d73-455d-9fd1-5e66c268aba5)

Item model file: https://github.com/baileyholl/Ars-Nouveau/blob/1.20/src/main/resources/assets/ars_nouveau/models/item/enchanters_sword.json

Sword geo model: 
https://github.com/baileyholl/Ars-Nouveau/blob/1.20/src/main/resources/assets/ars_nouveau/geo/sword.geo.json


Reproduce with any geckolib geo item:
Make item model without rotations
Make item with dramatic rotations for GUI
Expected: should render with brightness from the same angle for both items like in 1.19

Differing rendertypes don't matter, the only reproduction is to take the same item model and remove rotations, and it will render with correct vanilla lighting again.

Hello,

I am experiencing an issue with the mining speed of my animated blocks in my mod. I am using the GeckoLib library to create the animations, and I have noticed that when I mine the blocks, the mining speed is significantly slower than it should be.

I have narrowed down the issue to the use of the GeckoLib library, as when I remove the animations and use regular blocks, the mining speed is normal.

I would appreciate it if someone from the GeckoLib development team could provide some insight into why this might be happening and if there is a solution.

Thank you.

Removing all Mods besides Geckolib and the Mods which uses it still leads to crashes. With only Geckolib and Vinery (which worked fine before) or Naturalist, it keeps crashing. Only Geckolib works fine.

issues.title: (Quilt/1.19/Kotlin) Add register method in ItemRegistry
issues.body:
This code in the example item registry seems to be preventing me from using geckolib in quilt 1.19.3 (geckolib 4.0.2).
```java
public static final JackInTheBoxItem JACK_IN_THE_BOX = registerItem("jack_in_the_box", new JackInTheBoxItem(new Item.Settings()));
```

Correct me if I'm wrong but I had the same issue with my own mod items and it turns out you need to set the item field to the return value of Registry.register. Not sure why the fabric wiki does not reflect this...

```java
// In ItemRegistry
public static final JackInTheBoxItem JACK_IN_THE_BOX = null;

public static void register() {
 JACK_IN_THE_BOX = registerItem("jack_in_the_box", new JackInTheBoxItem(new Item.Settings()));
}

// In the ModInitializer implementation
public void onInitialize(ModContainer mod) {
    ItemRegistry.register();
}

```

issues.title: Entities using GeoEntityRenderer still render when being invisible
issues.body:
Invisibility potions don't affect mobs or entities extending GeoEntityRenderer.
The reason is because mobs by default have renderType entityCutout which ignores the alpha value in the renderRecursively method. 
https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/a6830ed2191f90e36a5cb8797474f0dd88e0d33e/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib3/renderers/geo/GeoEntityRenderer.java#L149
An easier solution to this, is to simply move the check to the shouldRender method or do the boolean check for the whole render call:
```
if(entity.isInvisibleTo(Minecraft.getInstance().player)) render(model, entity, partialTicks, renderType, stack, bufferIn, null, packedLightIn,
				getPackedOverlay(entity, 0), (float) renderColor.getRed() / 255f, (float) renderColor.getGreen() / 255f,
				(float) renderColor.getBlue() / 255f, invis ? 0.0F : (float) renderColor.getAlpha() / 255);
```
You might as well use the method isVisible that is sitting there not doing anything.
This line:
https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/a6830ed2191f90e36a5cb8797474f0dd88e0d33e/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib3/renderers/geo/GeoEntityRenderer.java#L231
instead of rewriting entity.isInvisibleTo.

issues.title: [Fabric 1.18] combining animations ?
Replace GeckoLibMod.DISABLE_IN_DEV with a system property
issues.body:
The current approach requires mods wishing to disable the examples to load before GeckoLib. 
This is impossible to consistently achieve for Fabric mods, as Fabric deliberately loads mod entrypoints in an arbitrary order relative to other mods. 
Using a system property (via `java.lang.Boolean.getBoolean(String)`) would be a much better approach, as system properties can be set via VM launch arguments.

issues.title: [1.17.x Fabric] Entity animations with sound effects bug if the shouldLoop animation field is set to false
[1.17.x Fabric] Sound events in animated items are fired for all observers, rather than just the owner
issues.body:
One thing curious I noticed about how GeckoLib handles sound keyframe events is that they are fired for *every player who is observing the animation*, rather than only firing the event for the item's owner. This makes implementing sounds with one singular source difficult with proper attenuation.

Currently one fix may be to add a check on whether the player is triggering the event (e.g. in my case, using the gravity gun). This might work for one user with multiple observers, but when two users are firing at the same time, they will receive and accept each other's events and so the sound will double. So IMO without fixing this from GeckoLib's side, this problem cannot be sidestepped.

issues.title: [Forge 1.16.5] getRenderType and getRenderColor are redundant and useless in ItemGeoRenderer
issues.body:
Starting from this line:
https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/549fbe9d5648528aac0c0183580aaecbdf739b1c/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib3/renderers/geo/GeoItemRenderer.java#L98
The two methods mentioned in the title are useless and don't get called. There are two identically named methods in IGeoRenderer that are used in the render method instead.
https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/blob/549fbe9d5648528aac0c0183580aaecbdf739b1c/src/main/java/software/bernie/geckolib3/renderers/geo/IGeoRenderer.java#L113
While these two methods don't hurt or crash anything, they are quite confusing since overriding them instead of the IGeoRenderer's ones will not run the code.
If you can possibly delete these two methods, it would make it clearer which to use.

issues.title: [Forge 1.16.5] Non-Array Custom Instruction Keyframes Causing Crash
issues.body:
Geckolib seems to expect all custom instruction keyframes to be defined in the animation jsons as lists, and will crash otherwise. Here is the crash log: [https://pastebin.com/qzRcn02N](https://pastebin.com/qzRcn02N)

Blockbench saves single-instruction keyframes as singletons, however:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7550579/125340003-ecb97300-e31f-11eb-9ccc-1407a1ec0c61.png)
This can be easily circumvented by manually placing each script into a list. But animation files are edited and saved over in Blockbench frequently, requiring these corrections to be reapplied each time.

issues.title: The current version isn't working with 1.16.4
issues.body:
The current version updates in 1.16.4 but when you try to load it the thing requires a version of forge that you can only pick for a 1.16.5 mod pack in the forge loader. 

[crash-2021-04-22_07.58.03-fml.txt](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/files/6358052/crash-2021-04-22_07.58.03-fml.txt)

As you can see it's asking for forge 36.1.1 but the highest forge level supported by 1.16.4 in the options list is 35.1.37

![version](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24589533/115712114-5e49dc80-a342-11eb-9f37-f0fa1199d282.png)

It won't let me choose a higher version number. I considered just updating the pack to 1.16.5 but not all of the mods I'm using are there yet. At the moment I've backed gecko all the way to the last 1.16.4 specific version and will be testing further versions one by until until I get the crash again but . . . I figured you'd want to know the problem exists. 

Having the update arrow stuck there isn't game breaking, but it is annoying when I can't actually update. lol

Edit - I can get it to work without the crash all the way up to 1.16.5-3.0.31,  So it looks like it's only the two versions that came out in this last week that aren't backwards compatible.

issues.title: this crash on servers with forge-1.16.3-geckolib-2.1.2.jar
bad packaging
issues.body:
forge-1.16.3-geckolib-3.0.0-beta.2.jar

This jar is poorly named, making it hard to find in an alphabetical list of jar files when you're looking for "geckolib".
It should be something like this:

geckolib-forge-1.16.3-3.0.0-beta.2.jar

Also, it has a pack.mcmeta file, but it's the default examplemod version.  This information shows up during game creation when choosing datapacks, and could also be helpful during debugging, if it were correctly set, but as is, it's pretty useless, and only adds to a player's confusion when things don't work.

And, you're missing the META-INF/mods.toml file, which provides mod id, version, and dependency information.  It's absence causes problems for other mods, such as Ars Nouveau ( https://github.com/baileyholl/Ars-Nouveau/issues/54#issue-735738948 ).

issues.body:
Hey, since GeckoLib is an official sponsor of Modtoberfest, I figured I'd setup a few good issues people can work on.

This one should be pretty easy. Basically we need to add more in-depth and commented examples to GeckoLib so people have a better reference.

Good example ideas:
- An entity with several attacks on a timer
- An entity with several animation controllers running multiple animations simultaneously
- An entity with many animations such as walking, flying, idle, sleeping, eating, attacking, and a death animation
- A tile entity animation with several animations
- Basically anything creative that makes good use of geckolib's features and is preferably commented 

Make sure you're on the [develop ](https://github.com/bernie-g/geckolib/tree/develop)branch

Thank you for contributing and using geckolib!
